summary: self-certificates ships a base64-obfuscated remote-fetch-and-exec payload disguised as a PEM test key
details: The package's test/key.pem is not an RSA key: its armored body decodes through two layers of base64 into an async IIFE that fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response body into python3 (or python on win32) via child_process.spawn with detached:true and windowsHide:true. index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the PEM armor, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting string to selfsign.generate() from the self-sign dependency as a third argument, causing the decoded payload to be executed when a consumer imports self-certificates and calls generateCertificates(). The exfil URL is itself stored base64-encoded inside the payload. The combination of a two-layer base64 blob armored as an RSA PRIVATE KEY, a hidden base64-encoded remote URL, detached/windowsHide child-process spawning, and cover-story framing as a test key has no legitimate role in a certificate-generation library and results in arbitrary code execution on the installer's host under attacker control.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
